qualitative_findings.claim: dsDNA monolayers transmit predominantly negatively polarized electrons independent of light polarization (linear, cw, ccw).
Absolute spin polarization tends to increase with dsDNA length (26-78 bp).
No net spin selectivity for ssDNA monolayers or UV-damaged dsDNA.
With ccw light the |P| of dsDNA increases slightly because injected electrons are pre-polarized in the filter's preferred direction.
Polarization is energy independent within Ekin = 0-1.2 eV.
Total photoelectron yield through 50 bp dsDNA is ~7% larger for ccw than cw light (circular dichroism), independent of kinetic energy.

discrepancies.description: Main text: dsDNA 'thiolated on the 3′ end of one of the DNA strands'. SI: 78 bp duplex carries SH-(CH2)6 on the 5′ end of the bottom strand (also primer). Recorded per SI.
Fig. 1 caption: DNA-transmitted (negative P) electrons have spin antiparallel to velocity. Fig. 2A caption: cw light gives -22% and 'spin ... parallel (green)'. These imply opposite sign meanings.
Pulse duration ~200 ps (main) vs ~300 ps fundamental (SI); photon energy 5.84 eV (main/SI p.3) vs 5.9 eV (Fig. S6 caption).
SI states 'ratio of major to minor axes ... about 0.96'; a value < 1 corresponds to minor/major.
Fig. 4 averages are the only multi-preparation data and are graphical only; per-length sample counts not given (12 samples, 40 experiments total).

discrepancies.field: cross-paper sign of bare Au(111) circular-light polarization
discrepancies.description: Here cw light on Au(111) gives -22%; Möllers 2021 reports ~+25% for cw on Au(111) with the same apparatus family. Helicity/sign conventions are not harmonized across papers.

extraction_meta.notes: Science pages 894-897 (PDF also contains unrelated neighbouring articles). SI cited by printed page numbers. Fig. 4 points are to_digitize. Duplex handedness/helix form not stated in this paper and left not_reported.
